notes: Replace update-positional-first-match with update-positional-query-array-binding to avoid repeating the projection first-match fact. Replace group-addtoset-unique-values with group-addtoset-single-value-array, and lookup-equality-field-pair with lookup-array-local-scalar-foreign, to avoid name giveaways and definition cards.

cards.statement: MongoDB matches {"profile.city":"Rome"} against the city field inside an embedded profile document.
cards.explanation: The dot path "profile.city" addresses the city field within profile. Other fields inside that embedded document can remain present.

cards.statement: MongoDB's query equality treats embedded documents with reordered fields and the same values as equal.
cards.explanation: An equality predicate on a whole embedded document compares field order as well as field names and values.
cards.misconception: Embedded-document equality ignores the order of fields.

cards.statement: MongoDB can match {tags:"blue"} against a document whose tags array contains "blue".
cards.explanation: A scalar equality predicate on tags succeeds when an array element equals "blue". Additional array elements can remain present.

cards.statement: The query {tags:["blue","green"]} matches a document whose tags value is ["green","blue"].
cards.explanation: An array-valued equality predicate compares the element sequence. Reversing those elements produces a different array value.
cards.misconception: Array-valued equality treats arrays as unordered sets.

cards.statement: MongoDB's query {tags:{$all:["blue","green"]}} matches a document with tags:["blue","green","red"].
cards.explanation: Query $all checks that its listed values occur in the field. The matching array can also contain additional values.

cards.statement: The query $size predicate can select arrays whose lengths fall within a specified range.
cards.explanation: Query $size accepts a single exact array length. It rejects a range condition as its argument.
cards.misconception: Query $size accepts range comparisons on array length.

cards.statement: Query $elemMatch requires an array element to satisfy its combined query conditions.
cards.explanation: Query $elemMatch binds the conditions inside it to one element. Separate elements satisfying different conditions are insufficient.

cards.statement: A find() projection can combine {name:1} with {status:0} in the same projection document.
cards.explanation: A find() projection uses inclusion or exclusion for ordinary fields. The _id field provides the exception that permits mixing those modes.
cards.misconception: find() freely mixes inclusion and exclusion for ordinary fields.

cards.statement: MongoDB's positional $ projection returns the first array element matching the query condition.
cards.explanation: Positional $ projection returns a one-element array containing the first qualifying element. It omits later qualifying elements.

cards.statement: Projection $elemMatch requires its condition to be present in the find() filter.
cards.explanation: Projection $elemMatch takes an explicit element-selection condition. That condition can differ from the filter selecting documents.
cards.misconception: Projection $elemMatch derives its condition from the document filter.

cards.statement: MongoDB interprets a negative scalar $slice projection argument as a request for an array's first elements.
cards.explanation: A negative scalar projection $slice argument selects the last elements of the array, using the argument's absolute value as the requested count.
cards.misconception: A negative projection $slice count starts at the beginning of the array.

cards.statement: A find() projection can compute a new field using an aggregation expression.
cards.explanation: find() accepts aggregation expressions in its projection document. The returned field takes the expression's computed value.

cards.statement: updateOne() advances to another match when its first match already has the requested field values.
cards.explanation: updateOne() selects one matching document. A no-op on that document ends the operation rather than advancing to another match needing a change.
cards.misconception: updateOne() searches for a matching document that needs an actual modification.

cards.statement: replaceOne() keeps an existing status field when its replacement omits the status field.
cards.explanation: replaceOne() replaces the document's content with the replacement. Old non-_id fields omitted from that replacement disappear.
cards.misconception: replaceOne() merges replacement fields into the existing document.

cards.statement: Update $set can change "profile.city" while keeping sibling fields in an embedded profile document.
cards.explanation: Using a dot path in update $set changes the selected nested field. Existing sibling fields inside profile remain intact.

cards.statement: MongoDB removes status when update $unset specifies {status:""} for a document containing that field.
cards.explanation: In {$unset:{status:""}}, the empty string is an ignored operand value. MongoDB removes the status field from the document.

cards.statement: MongoDB creates a missing counter field with the increment value when update $inc targets it.
cards.explanation: Update $inc initializes a missing field to the supplied increment value, so a counter can begin with that first increment.

cards.statement: updateMany() with upsert:true can insert a new document alongside documents matched by that operation.
cards.explanation: With upsert:true, updateMany() updates documents that match its filter. It inserts a new document when the filter finds no match.
cards.misconception: An upsert inserts a new document even when the filter finds existing matches.

cards.statement: The $push update operator can append a direct array operand as separate array elements.
cards.explanation: Update $push appends a literal array operand as one nested array element. The $each modifier supplies values to append separately.
cards.misconception: A literal array operand to $push spreads its elements into the target array.

cards.statement: The $addToSet update operator can remove duplicate values already present in its target array.
cards.explanation: Update $addToSet avoids adding an existing value, but leaves duplicate values already present in the array unchanged.
cards.misconception: Update $addToSet cleans up duplicates already stored in an array.

cards.statement: The $pull update operator removes matching values throughout the target array.
cards.explanation: Update $pull tests the array's elements against its removal condition. Matching values are removed wherever they occur in that array.

cards.statement: A positional $ update requires its array field to appear in the query that selects the document.
cards.explanation: For a positional $ update, the query includes the targeted array field. MongoDB derives the array position to update from that query match.

cards.statement: The $[] update operator uses arrayFilters to select which array elements it changes.
cards.explanation: $[] targets elements throughout the named array. Use $[<identifier>] with arrayFilters to select elements by a condition.
cards.misconception: The empty positional brackets use arrayFilters in the same way as filtered positional identifiers.

cards.statement: An updateOne() pipeline update can include a $project stage to reshape the matched document.
cards.explanation: Pipeline updates accept $addFields/$set, $project/$unset and $replaceRoot/$replaceWith. This restricted stage subset reshapes the selected document.

cards.statement: An aggregation $match on total reads the total produced by an earlier $set stage.
cards.explanation: A pipeline passes stage output onward. Later predicates evaluate the current document shape produced by preceding stages.

cards.statement: The aggregation stage { $match: { status: "open" } } retains each matching document's other fields.
cards.explanation: $match passes matching input documents onward intact. Fields outside its predicate remain in the output documents.

cards.statement: An aggregation $project expression can make a field absent depending on that input document's data.
cards.explanation: A $project field expression that yields $$REMOVE omits that field. A conditional expression chooses whether to return $$REMOVE for a particular document.

cards.statement: An aggregation $set stage preserves an existing status: "old" after { $set: { status: "new" } }.
cards.explanation: The aggregation $set stage overwrites an existing field with its expression's value. Setting status to "new" replaces the previous status value.
cards.misconception: The aggregation $set stage adds fields but preserves values when those fields already exist.

cards.statement: An aggregation $limit before $sort selects its input documents according to the later sort's ranking.
cards.explanation: $limit first selects an incoming subset, then $sort orders that subset. Sorting descending before limiting selects the highest scores from the full input.
cards.misconception: MongoDB sorts the complete aggregation input before applying $limit regardless of stage order.

cards.statement: In aggregation expressions, "$price" represents a literal string because it appears inside quotes.
cards.explanation: In an aggregation expression, "$price" reads the price field. Use { $literal: "$price" } to return that string unchanged.
cards.misconception: Ordinary string quotation prevents MongoDB from interpreting a leading dollar sign as a field path.

cards.statement: The aggregation $out stage replaces an existing output collection's documents when it succeeds.
cards.explanation: A successful $out replaces the existing destination with the pipeline results, so earlier destination documents outside those results disappear.

cards.statement: In a sharded cluster, the aggregation $merge stage can write its results to a sharded collection.
cards.explanation: $merge accepts a sharded destination collection. A pipeline can persist its results across the shards of that collection.

cards.statement: db.items.aggregate([{ $set: { flag: true } }]) can persist flag in the items collection.
cards.explanation: An aggregation containing {$set:{flag:true}} reshapes pipeline documents. It leaves stored source documents unchanged.
cards.misconception: An aggregation $set stage also updates the stored source documents.

cards.statement: With allowDiskUse: true, an aggregation $sort stage can spill excess stage memory to temporary files.
cards.explanation: When an aggregation sort needs more than its stage memory allowance, enabling allowDiskUse permits it to write intermediate data to disk.

cards.statement: In MongoDB 9.0, allowDiskUse: true lets an aggregation exceed its per-operation memory limit.
cards.explanation: MongoDB 9.0 caps the combined tracked memory for one operation even when disk spilling is enabled.
cards.misconception: Enabling disk spilling removes the combined operation memory budget.
cards.volatilityNote: The per-operation budget is new in MongoDB 9.0 and its enforcement may evolve in later releases.

cards.statement: MongoDB enforces the returned-document BSON size limit on intermediate aggregation documents.
cards.explanation: Intermediate pipeline documents may exceed the BSON result-document size limit. MongoDB checks returned result documents against that limit.
cards.misconception: MongoDB applies the returned-document BSON size restriction at each intermediate pipeline stage.

cards.statement: The $group stage puts the chosen group key in each output document's _id field.
cards.explanation: The $group stage evaluates its _id expression to identify groups, then includes that value in the _id field of the group's result.

cards.statement: The $group stage returns its grouped documents in ascending order of their _id values.
cards.explanation: The $group stage leaves group order unspecified. Add a following $sort stage when the order of groups matters.
cards.misconception: Grouping by a key also sorts the resulting groups by that key.

cards.statement: In the $group stage, { $sum: 1 } accumulates a document count per group.
cards.explanation: Within $group, the accumulator { $sum: 1 } adds one for each input document assigned to a group, producing that group's document count.

cards.statement: The $avg accumulator in $group treats null inputs as zero when calculating its average.
cards.explanation: The $avg accumulator in $group ignores null and other nonnumeric inputs, so they contribute neither a value nor an item to the average.
cards.misconception: The $avg accumulator includes null inputs in the average as zero-valued entries.

cards.statement: The $push accumulator in $group follows the order of documents entering that stage.
cards.explanation: Within $group, $push builds its result array in input-document order. Sort before grouping to establish the desired array order.

cards.statement: In $group, $addToSet returns a scalar when the group has one distinct value.
cards.explanation: The $addToSet accumulator in $group returns an array of distinct expression results. One distinct value still produces a one-element array.
cards.misconception: The $addToSet accumulator unwraps a result containing one distinct value into a scalar.

cards.statement: The $lookup stage matches elements of an array-valued localField against scalar foreignField values.
cards.explanation: When localField contains an array, $lookup matches its elements to scalar foreignField values. The join works directly on that array-valued local field.

cards.statement: The $lookup stage emits a separate local document for each matching foreign document.
cards.explanation: The $lookup stage keeps a local document and places its matching foreign documents in the array named by as.
cards.misconception: The $lookup stage multiplies local documents instead of collecting foreign matches in an array.

cards.statement: Inside a $lookup foreign pipeline, "$qty" directly references qty in the outer input document.
cards.explanation: A field path such as "$qty" reads from the foreign pipeline document. Bind outer fields with let and reference those variables as "$$name".
cards.misconception: Field paths inside a $lookup foreign pipeline directly address fields of the outer input document.

cards.statement: In a sharded cluster, the $lookup stage accepts a sharded foreign collection.
cards.explanation: A $lookup stage accepts a sharded collection in its from field. Distributing that foreign collection across shards preserves its eligibility for the join.

cards.statement: The aggregation $unwind stage returns each scalar array element as a bare result value.
cards.explanation: The $unwind stage emits documents carrying the input document's other fields, with the selected array field replaced by one element.
cards.misconception: The $unwind stage returns bare element values instead of documents that retain the other input fields.

cards.statement: With preserveNullAndEmptyArrays: true, $unwind retains a document whose selected field is missing.
cards.explanation: The $unwind stage keeps a document with a missing path when preserveNullAndEmptyArrays is true, and the path stays absent in the output.
